answer: A bonded peer interview panel makes fakes face live humans, not scripts. First, three random veterans lock 10 POA each and grill the newcomer for eight minutes on a copper timer. Second, questions are drawn fresh from a basalt-hard seed so rehearsed clones fail. Third, a unanimous fail burns the applicant's 40 POA deposit; a pass refunds both sides. Fourth, each veteran may sit only two panels a week. Running 500 fakes means hiring actors at about $30 each plus 20,000 POA at risk, near $35,000 per wave. It is like cracking a walnut: one hard shell, one kernel, no room for twins.
